claim: Human choices mix model-free and model-based control in the two-step task; median model-free weight 61% (N=17), so pure model-free RPE learning is not the whole story.
agent_test: Compare agent with a plain reward-history policy vs one that uses an explicit transition model on a two-step text task at equal tokens.

claim: Ventral striatum BOLD carries both model-free RPE and model-based value information, so the RPE signal is not purely model-free.
agent_test: Not directly testable; background.

claim: In rodents, optogenetic dopamine transients can drive new learning (sensory preconditioning, value gain) but evidence on whether they act as model-free errors is split: Sharpe 2017/2020 say no (cue-to-cue links), Maes 2020 says dopamine silencing impairs second-order conditioning as TD predicts.
agent_test: Background; no agent test.

claim: Dopamine neurons in mice show diverse reversal points (optimistic and pessimistic cells), consistent with distributional RL; split-half R=0.58, p=1.8e-5, 40 neurons from 5 mice. Reanalysed data, small cell counts per animal; Avvisati 2024 found extra structure by projection target.
agent_test: Have the agent keep a spread of outcome estimates (optimistic and pessimistic) rather than one mean for repeated choices; compare regret at equal tokens.

claim: Dopamine release patterns (ramps, cue responses rising with experience) challenge the uniform classic TD-RPE account; competing accounts (value-ramp RPE, retrospective causal learning) fit some data each.
agent_test: Background.

claim: Fitted RL parameters in humans have poor test-retest reliability (ICC .02 to .52 bandit, .01 to .71 reversal) while win-stay is more stable (ICC .53 to .62).
agent_test: Warns against using fitted learning rates as stable agent traits; use behavioural indices.

claim: A sparse-autoencoder latent in Llama block 34 correlates r=0.58 with a Q-learning TD error, and lesioning it hurts performance (next-state accuracy 24.3% to 18.9%, ceiling 25%). Moderate correlation, single open model, preprint. Re-verified against the PDF. Different-method support: Zou 2026 finds sparse value and TD-error probe neurons in Qwen and Llama models; this is convergent evidence, not a replication of the SAE latent.
agent_test: Ablate TD-like latents in an open model and measure effect on in-context bandit tasks.

claim: LLMs learn in context from reward feedback with asymmetric updating: alpha+ 0.87 vs alpha- 0.10 (Claude v1.3, 50 runs) and confirmatory 0.483 vs disconfirmatory 0.166 across four chat models (1,200 runs): an optimism or confirmation bias like humans.
agent_test: Run the same partial-feedback bandit with and without a rule to weight failures equally; measure regret at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show relative-value encoding: GPT-4 Turbo chooses the locally optimal option about 99% by trial 5 but is biased when payoffs are relative; bias persists in comparison framings (.829 vs .698 relative-value choice rate).
agent_test: Present options in absolute vs relative framing; measure choice accuracy.

claim: In-context reward feedback improves LLM performance: Banking77 Qwen2.5-7B 6.2% to 72.2% (stochastic ICRL), and Game of 24 GPT-4.1 90% (ICRL preset) vs Best-of-N 49%, Reflexion 44%. Both re-verified. Caveats: self-judged reward on Game of 24, compute budgets differ, one model per benchmark. Caveat (gap search): Kwon 2026 finds the gain comes mostly from showing earlier attempts, not from the reward value (flipped or random rewards keep most of the gain).
agent_test: Run a reward-annotated multi-episode loop vs best-of-N at matched total tokens on a verifiable task.

claim: LLMs in-context RL is fragile: naive ICRL is unstable, negative-reward learning is weak, and positive-only context works best.
agent_test: Test whether including failed attempts helps or hurts at equal tokens.

claim: Reward-aware attention heads exist: 597 of 2,048 heads (29.1%) significant vs 102 expected by chance (249 positive, 348 negative), one model, creative writing only.
agent_test: Background.

claim: Unaided LLMs explore poorly in bandits: GPT-4 basic prompt had suffix failure in over 60% of replicates; success needed an external summary; Gemini results show UCB (90.6 to 96.4% win rate) beats raw-history prompting (27.7 to 45.5%). Reasoning models later raised directed exploration (Zhang 2025), not on a common metric.
agent_test: Give the agent an algorithmic summary (counts, means) instead of raw history; measure win rate at equal tokens.

claim: Transformers can implement TD(0) in the forward pass in theory (policy evaluation, linear attention, small synthetic MRPs).
agent_test: Background.

claim: Scale and prompting raise model-basedness in LLMs: parameters beta=0.481; chain-of-thought +64.59%, step-back +118.59% on a model-basedness score (35 LLMs, temperature 0).
agent_test: Add a planning or step-back step before choosing in a two-step task; compare to none at equal tokens.

claim: A prediction-error-style gate for agent memory (D-MEM) cut tokens 80% (319K vs 1,648K) with F1 0.369 vs 0.336 on noisy LoCoMo, but single-hop F1 fell (21.6 vs 44.7) and the gate is embedding surprise, not a reward error.
agent_test: Gate memory writes by surprise vs write-all at equal tokens, scoring single- and multi-hop questions separately.

claim: Centaur, fine-tuned on human choice data, beats domain cognitive models on average (NLL 0.44 vs 0.56) but not in all experiments (horizon task worse).
agent_test: Background.

claim: Direct in-context RL gains come mostly from the earlier attempts shown in context, not from the reward label: flipped, random or removed rewards keep most of the gain (HumanEval+, MBPP+, ScienceWorld; six small models). Reward-sensitive improvement is 3.3% (HumanEval+) and 4.4% (MBPP+) of model-problem cells.
agent_test: Run a retry loop with true, flipped and no score labels on a verifiable task at equal tokens; check whether the label matters for a frontier model.

claim: Raw failed attempts in context are replayed, not avoided: showing a failed trajectory raises its replay from 0.7% to 3.1%, and its low reward label only lowers this to 2.5%. Reflexion-style verbal reflection plus a reliable test signal does help (HumanEval Rust hard 50: 0.60 to 0.68), and removing the test signal hurts (0.52).
agent_test: A/B: raw failed attempts versus a one-sentence reflection of each failure versus nothing, same token budget, external verifier.

claim: A multi-attempt loop whose reward is a majority-vote pseudo-label beats best-of-16 on math at a stated fixed budget (Qwen2.5-7B: MATH 71.0 vs 69.6, AMC 53.0 vs 43.4), but spurious rewards lower accuracy and later rounds degrade as context grows. Not shown for an external verifier at matched tokens.
agent_test: Compare reward-annotated loop with best-of-N at matched tokens on a task with a hard verifier.

claim: LLM optimism asymmetry depends on what the scaffold shows: it is limited to free choices, reverses for the unchosen option under full feedback, and disappears for another agent's forced choices; adding such observed outcomes cut regret from 0.07 to 0.02 (t(143)=2.5). One model (Claude v1.3, temperature 0). No direct debiasing prompt was found in the literature.
agent_test: Test counterfactual or observed-others feedback in a bandit-like text task on current models.

claim: Value-like and TD-error-like signals are linearly readable from LLM hidden states in several open models, and zeroing under 1% of value neurons cuts MATH500 from 75.2% to 37.0% (layer 2), while a dopamine-neuron process reward lifts best-of-4 MATH500 to 72.3% average versus 66.1% random. Authors call the causal evidence preliminary.
agent_test: Not testable through a black-box API; note only.

claim: Computing summary statistics or UCB-style guidance outside the model and writing it into the prompt helps larger models and contextual bandits (Gemini Pro CB 7.1 to 64.3 win-rate) but hurts the smallest (Gemma-2B 7.6 to 4.9). No evidence outside bandits was found.
agent_test: Try externally computed counts in a multi-step reasoning scaffold with a strong model.

claim: Dopamine neurons in two monkeys encoded the current reward minus a recency-weighted average of past rewards, but only for positive errors (44 of 50 neurons modulated at p<0.01, mean R-squared 0.29; below-baseline firing carried no history signal). Contested later.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: The RPE theory in its original form is too simple (ramping, sensory and motor responses, action selection, backward blocking, uncertainty). Generalised prediction-error accounts answer many challenges but some findings need other explanations.
agent_test: Background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Levodopa (150 mg, N=62, within-subject) boosted model-based guidance of model-free credit assignment without a direct effect on model-based or model-free choice; model-agnostic analyses were partly null. No replication found.
agent_test: Background only.
